I added the `bulk-refunds` flag and gated `refund()` on it. I haven't run the code or any tests.

- **`flags.toml`:** I declared `bulk-refunds = false`, so the flag is off by default. Per the project convention, a flag has to be declared there before code reads it.
- **`src/billing/refunds.py`:** `refund()` now checks `flags.is_on("bulk-refunds")` first. If the flag is off, it raises `RuntimeError("refunds are disabled: bulk-refunds flag is off")`.

Because the flag defaults to off, every existing `refund()` call will now raise until you turn it on. I chose to raise rather than return quietly because a silent no-op on a refund could hide a failure. If you'd rather it return `None` or fall back to some other behavior, that's a small change.

I didn't save anything to memory, since nothing came up that wasn't already in the feature-flag convention.
